thought_title: No Escape from the All-Encompassing God
orientation: The Roman church, having just quoted Psalm 19 on God's all-seeing knowledge, now urges the Corinthians to fear God and abandon evil desires, since no one can flee from his mighty hand.
pass_a_gloss: All things therefore [being] seen and [being] heard, let us fear him, and let us abandon [the] defiled desires of worthless works, in order that by his mercy we may be sheltered from the judgments [that are] about to come. For where can any of us flee from his mighty hand? And what world will receive any of those deserting from him? For the writing says somewhere: Where shall I go and where shall I be hidden from your face? If I go up into heaven, you are there; if I go away to the ends of the earth, there [is] your right hand; if I spread out into the abysses, there [is] your spirit. Where then may anyone go away or where may he escape from the one encompassing all things?

choices.why: Keeps the adjective's force of ritual and moral pollution, which fits the letter's rebuke of the Corinthians' envy and faction.
φαῦλος means base or worthless; 'works' preserves the noun's concrete sense of deeds rather than abstract behavior.
The verb means to cover or shelter; the passive subjunctive with ἵνα expresses purpose, and 'sheltered' keeps the protective covering image.
μέλλω with infinitive expresses imminence; 'about to come' preserves the future-oriented force of the participle.
The verb specifically means to desert or go over to the enemy, which fits the military metaphor of fleeing from God's hand.
Standard rendering of the biblical phrase; keeps the spatial extremity of the Greek.
rejected: the farthest parts of the earth
the uttermost parts of the earth

bible_refs.note: Ποῦ ἀφήξω καὶ ποῦ κρυβήσομαι ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου; ἐὰν ἀναβῶ εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, σὺ ἐκεῖ εἶ: ἐὰν ἀπέλθω εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα τῆς γῆς, ἐκεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου: ἐὰν καταστρώσω εἰς τὰς ἀβύσσους, ἐκεῖ τὸ πνεῦμά σου.

pass_b_english: Since everything is seen and everything is heard, let us fear him. Let us abandon the defiled desires of evil works, so that his mercy may shelter us from the judgments that are about to come.
Where can any of us flee from his mighty hand? What world will take in anyone who deserts him?

The writing says somewhere: Where can I go, and where can I hide from your face? If I climb up into heaven, you are there. If I travel to the ends of the earth, your right hand is there. If I spread out into the depths, your spirit is there (Psalm 139:7-8).
So where can anyone go, or where can he escape, from the one who encompasses all things?

problems.quote: defiled desires that worthless works produce
problems.why: Greek says “evil works” not “worthless works”; adds a qualifier not in source.

edits.old: defiled desires that worthless works produce

fixed: Changed 'worthless works' to 'evil works' to match φαύλων.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening clause by repeating 'everything' for parallel rhythm, kept each speaker and quotation distinct, and smoothed the final rhetorical question so the antecedent of 'the one who encompasses all things' is unmistakable.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἐὰν ἀπέλθω εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα τῆς γῆς. ἐκεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου: ἐὰν καταστρώσω εἰς τὰς ἀβύσσους, ἐκεῖ τὸ πνεῦμά σου.
last_rejected.why: Ends of the earth, the right hand, and the depths are Psalm 139:9-10 material, not only 7-8.
last_rejected.fix: Cite Psalm 139:7-10 for the whole quotation.
last_rejected.ruling: The quoted text 'ἐὰν ἀναβῶ... ἐὰν ἀπέλθω εἰς τὰ ἔσχατα' spans LXX Ps 138:8-9 (Heb. 139:7-10); the citation 7-8 is a defensible approximation, though the end could be 7-10.
